message.content:
In this Go codebase (memos), search for:

1. Webhook delivery system - find where outbound HTTP requests are made for webhooks, any URL validation/protection against SSRF (internal network addresses)
2. Attachment/resource system - find any background job that checks or refreshes external links/URLs for attachments/resources
3. Find any "s3" or external storage references and link freshness checks

Run these searches:
- grep -rn "http.Post\|http.Get\|http.Do\|httpClient\|http.Client" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -30
- grep -rn "webhook" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -40
- grep -rn "SSRF\|ssrf\|internal.*address\|private.*ip\|loopback\|127\.0\.\|10\.\|192\.168\|DisallowedHost\|allowedHost\|resolv" --include="*.go" -i . | head -20
- grep -rn "presign\|signed.*url\|signedurl\|link.*expire\|expire.*link\|stale\|refresh.*link\|refresh.*url\|external.*link" --include="*.go" -i . | head -20
- grep -rn "s3\|S3\|minio\|blob\|external.*storage\|object.*store" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -30
- grep -rn "ticker\|cron\|schedule\|interval\|periodic\|background.*job\|RunOnce" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -40
- grep -rn "presignedURL\|PreSignedURL\|presigned\|OutputPresign\|signedURL" --include="*.go" -i . | head -20

Read any key files you find. Report everything verbatim.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.description: Find webhook CRUD in the API layer
Find where webhook URL validation is called

content.text: Now let me read the full user_service_webhooks.go to see the complete webhook CRUD with validation.

Here is the complete report of findings.

---

## 1. Webhook Delivery System

### Outbound HTTP Requests

The webhook delivery system lives in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`. Outbound HTTP POST requests are made via a shared `safeClient` (`*http.Client`) at line 32, which uses a custom `Transport` with a `safeDialContext` function to guard against SSRF:

```go
safeClient = &http.Client{
    Timeout: timeout,
    Transport: &http.Transport{
        DialContext: safeDialContext,
    },
}
```

The `Post` function (line 119) marshals a `WebhookRequestPayload` to JSON, constructs an `http.NewRequest("POST", ...)`, optionally signs it with HMAC-SHA256 using Standard Webhooks headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`), and sends via `safeClient.Do(req)` (line 152).

Asynchronous dispatch is handled by `PostAsync` (line 182), which enqueues into a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128). Four goroutines consume from this channel (started in `init()`, line 43).

### SSRF Protection

**File: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`**

There are two layers of SSRF protection:

**Layer 1 -- URL Validation at webhook creation/update time** (`ValidateURL`, line 62):
- Parses the URL; requires `http` or `https` scheme.
- Calls `net.LookupHost` on the hostname.
- Checks every resolved IP against `reservedCIDRs` via `isReservedIP`.

**Layer 2 -- Connection-time dial guard** (`safeDialContext` in `webhook.go`, line 59):
- Before every outbound connection, the custom `DialContext` resolves the hostname again and rejects any IP in reserved ranges. This defeats DNS rebinding attacks where a hostname resolves to a public IP at validation time but re-resolves to a private IP at connection time.

The reserved CIDR list (line 14) covers:
- `127.0.0.0/8` (IPv4 loopback)
- `10.0.0.0/8` (RFC-1918 class A)
- `172.16.0.0/12` (RFC-1918 class B)
- `192.168.0.0/16` (RFC-1918 class C)
- `169.254.0.0/16` (link-local, including cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254)
- `::1/128` (IPv6 loopback)
- `fc00::/7` (IPv6 unique local)
- `fe80::/10` (IPv6 link-local)

The protection can be disabled via the package-level variable `AllowPrivateIPs` (line 41). When set to `true`, `isReservedIP` always returns `false`. This is described as useful for "self-hosted deployments where webhooks target services on the local network." Based on the grep results, `AllowPrivateIPs` is only set in test code (`webhook_test.go`); no production code sets it, so it defaults to `false` (SSRF protection enabled).

### Webhook Validation on Create/Update

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`**

`webhook.ValidateURL()` is called in three places:
- `CreateUserWebhook` (line 74): validates URL on creation.
- `UpdateUserWebhook` with field mask containing `"url"` (line 161): validates new URL.
- `UpdateUserWebhook` without field mask (line 182): validates if URL is non-empty.

Signing secrets are also validated via `webhook.ValidateSigningSecret()`.

### Webhook Dispatch Points

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`**

Four dispatch functions, all using `webhook.PostAsync`:
- `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` -- activity type `"memos.memo.created"`
- `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` -- activity type `"memos.memo.updated"`
- `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` -- activity type `"memos.memo.deleted"`
- `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` -- activity type `"memos.memo.comment.created"`

These are called from:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` lines 157 (created), 562 (deleted)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` line 67 (updated)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` line 119 (comment created)

---

## 2. Attachment/Resource System -- Background Job for External Link Refresh

### S3 Presign Runner (Background Job)

**File: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`**

This is the background job that refreshes S3 presigned URLs for attachments. Key details:

- **Interval**: Runs every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, line 27), using a `time.Ticker`.
- **Logic** (`CheckAndPresign`, line 47): Iterates through all S3-type attachments in batches of 100. For each attachment:
  - Checks `LastPresignedTime` in the S3 object payload.
  - **Skips if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days** (line 86-89). Since presigned URLs expire after 5 days, this means re-signing happens when the URL has 1 day or less of remaining validity.
  - Creates a new S3 client, calls `PresignGetObject`, and updates the attachment's `Reference` field with the new presigned URL and updates `LastPresignedTime`.

### Startup

**File: `/bench/repo/server/server.go` lines 153-174**

The S3 presign runner is started in `startBackgroundRunners`:
1. `RunOnce(ctx)` is called immediately at startup (line 163) to refresh any stale URLs.
2. A goroutine runs `Run(s3Context)` (line 169) for continuous 12-hour interval refreshes.
3. The runner has its own cancellable context (`s3Context`) for clean shutdown.

---

## 3. S3/External Storage References and Link Freshness

### S3 Client

**File: `/bench/repo/internal/storage/s3/s3.go`**

- Uses AWS SDK v2 (`aws-sdk-go-v2`).
- `PresignGetObject` (line 71) creates presigned URLs with a **5-day expiration** (line 79): `opts.Expires = time.Duration(5 * 24 * time.Hour)`.
- Supports `InsecureSkipTlsVerify` option (line 30) for self-signed S3 endpoints.
- Operations: `UploadObject`, `PresignGetObject`, `GetObject`, `GetObjectStream`, `DeleteObject`.

### Attachment Storage Flow

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go`**

When saving an S3 attachment (`SaveAttachmentBlob`, line 47):
1. Uploads blob to S3 via `s3Client.UploadObject`.
2. Immediately generates a presigned URL via `s3Client.PresignGetObject`.
3. Stores the presigned URL as `create.Reference`.
4. Records `LastPresignedTime: timestamppb.New(time.Now())` in the payload.

The `ExternalLink` field on attachments is populated from `attachment.Reference` for both `EXTERNAL` and `S3` storage types (line 39-41).

### On-demand Presigning (File Server)

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` lines 408-420**

`getS3PresignedURL` generates presigned URLs on-demand when serving files, creating a fresh S3 client and calling `PresignGetObject`.

### Attachment Payload Proto

**File: `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/attachment.pb.go`**

The `AttachmentPayload_S3Object` protobuf message has:
- `S3Config` -- the S3 configuration used.
- `Key` -- the S3 object key.
- `LastPresignedTime` -- timestamp of last presigning, used to determine if the presigned URL is still valid.

### Scheduler Package (Not Used for Presign Runner)

**File: `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/`**

A cron-based scheduler package exists (`scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`, `doc.go`) but the S3 presign runner does **not** use it -- it uses a simple `time.Ticker` loop instead. The scheduler package supports standard 5-field and 6-field cron expressions, middleware chains, and timezone-aware scheduling. No grep results showed it being used in the server startup flow for the presign runner.

### S3 Configuration Proto

**File: `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/instance_service.pb.go`**

`InstanceSetting_StorageSetting_S3Config` contains: `AccessKeyId`, `AccessKeySecret`, `Endpoint`, `Region`, `Bucket`, `UsePathStyle`, `InsecureSkipTlsVerify`.

---

### Summary of Key File Paths

- **Webhook delivery (outbound HTTP)**: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`
- **SSRF validation**: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`
- **Webhook CRUD API (with ValidateURL calls)**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`
- **Webhook dispatch from memo events**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`
- **S3 presign background runner**: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`
- **S3 client (presigned URL generation)**: `/bench/repo/internal/storage/s3/s3.go`
- **Attachment storage (S3 upload + initial presign)**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go`
- **File server (on-demand presign)**: `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
- **Background runner startup**: `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (lines 153-174)
- **Scheduler package (unused by presign runner)**: `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/`
- **Attachment payload proto (LastPresignedTime)**: `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/attachment.pb.go`
